extracted.intended_audience: academic researchers preparing manuscripts for journal submission (including early-career researchers and non-native English speakers)
extracted.subtask_short: avoiding desk rejection for journal submissions
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for authors to reduce the chance their manuscript is rejected at editorial triage (desk rejection) by ensuring fit, originality, rigour, and correct presentation before peer review. Focuses on journal selection, demonstrating novelty, methodological quality, and manuscript preparation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fit with journal aims and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers can be rejected for not fitting in with the journal’s mission and criteria; authors should select the appropriate journal for their article and ensure the paper is within the journal’s scope based on reputation and impact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Read the target journal’s objectives and scope carefully; read papers published in recent issues; choose the target journal before completing the manuscript; cite essential works showing how your study relates to the journal’s mission; highlight how your research relates to the journal’s readers and scope in the cover letter. (Article also suggests volunteering as a potential reviewer for the target journal.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and importance (novel contribution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals look for submissions that expand on concepts and present fresh theoretical perspectives; a paper that does not make an original contribution to knowledge or highlight its distinct contributions is unlikely to pass editorial triage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically analyse recent research and relevant theories to identify clear gaps to fill; use markers of originality such as new concepts, fresh approaches, fresh data, or expanding information into previously unrecognised dimensions; conduct an effective literature review (suggested focus on the past five years). Use the structured abstract and cover letter to underline novelty and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research rigour (methodological soundness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Research rigour refers to intellectual coherence and integrity, inclusion of sound concepts, analyses, sources, theories and procedures; faults in methods can trigger desk rejection even when topic and findings are interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid conceptual ambiguity, weak supporting evidence, and poor study methods. Ensure alignment between study aim and methodologies, high data quality, unbiased respondent selection, and suitable data analysis procedures with rigorous analysis. Fix methodological weaknesses before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear organisation, logical flow and argument clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript must meet quality criteria in organisation, argument clarity, logical flow and coherence; quality level will affect consideration for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a well-structured manuscript with clear, coherent arguments. Seek frank feedback from supervisors or trusted colleagues to improve organisation and clarity before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present and support claims with evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must provide evidence to back up any claims they make about new additions in their work; unsupported claims undermine perceived contribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critically analyse the literature and present data and argumentation that clearly support assertions of novelty and contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate novelty and significance in abstract and cover letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the structured abstract and cover letter to underline the novelty and significance of the research and how it relates to the journal’s readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the contribution explicit in the abstract; in the cover letter, describe the originality and significance and explicitly connect the manuscript to the journal’s scope and readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to journal/publisher formatting and style
rubrics_metrics.description: Most journals follow the publisher's format; papers should conform to that style and formatting requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the journal’s author guidelines and publisher formatting strictly to avoid triage on technical grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of plagiarism and similarity issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Some journals have strict requirements regarding text similarity and plagiarism; high similarity can lead to rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a text-similarity checking tool to spot potential plagiarism or overlap before submission and address issues appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language quality and copyediting
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor English or low-quality language can contribute to desk rejection; the manuscript must exhibit high standards of academic writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you struggle with English, hire a native speaker or reputable proofreading/copy-editing service to improve language quality and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective recent literature review
rubrics_metrics.description: A good literature review (recommended focus on the past five years) is necessary to position the study, identify gaps, and justify novelty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct an effective, up-to-date literature review to show how your work fills gaps and extends knowledge; this supports claims of originality and significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment of study aim and methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be a match between the study’s aim and the methodologies adopted; mismatches are a common reason for rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose methods appropriate to the research question and demonstrate why they are suitable; ensure methodological choices are coherent with stated aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data quality and sampling integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Poor data quality and potential bias in respondent selection can lead to desk rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure data are of high quality, sampling is appropriate and unbiased, and report limitations transparently where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission peer feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting frank feedback from a supervisor or trusted colleague can identify weaknesses and improve the manuscript before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask others to read your manuscript and give honest critique; incorporate suggested improvements to strengthen clarity, rigour and contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicitly connect study to journal readership and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors want to know why the journal’s readers would care about the work; the manuscript and cover letter should make this clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the cover letter and manuscript framing, highlight relevance to the journal’s audience, the study’s significance, and its potential impact or interest to readers.
